title.narrative: Saving lives and reducing the impact of disasters in urban areas: Strengthening Disaster preparedness and linking Early Warning to Early Action in Mzuzu, Blantyre, Lilongwe and Zomba City Councils

description.narrative:
Malawi is highly vulnerable to climate hazards ranging from floods, cyclones, and droughts, resulting in significant loss of lives and livelihood assets in urban and rural areas. In the recent past, urban areas have been hit by high intensity disasters including floods, heavy rains, and strong winds. To date, disaster management efforts in Malawi have predominantly focused on rural areas with urban areas receiving less attention and funding. 17.4% of Malawians live in urban areas and the urban population is projected to double by 2050, it is therefore critical to strengthen disaster risk management arrangements in the urban areas. Close to 80% of the urban population in Malawi resides in Lilongwe, Blantyre, Zomba and Mzuzu (NSO, 2009).
’Strengthening all-inclusive Disaster preparedness and linking Early Warning to Early Action in Mzuzu, Blantyre, Lilongwe, and Zomba City Councils" aims at enhancing the city council’s capacity to prepare for and respond to disasters. The project will target 376,811 beneficiaries (188,364 female and 188,447 male) in four prioritized wards in targeted cities (16 wards total). The project addresses disaster management issues in the urban areas, including high exposure to climate and non-climate risks, low adaptive capacity, gender, age and disability disparities; limited access to basic social and protection services; disaster preparedness capacity gaps, ineffective early warning systems, weak or absent civil protection committees, lack of contingency and evacuation plans; low rate of disaster risk management (DRM) policy implementation; and inadequate protection and shock-responsive social protection system (SRSPS).
The principal objective of the project is to protect livelihoods through enhanced all-inclusive disaster preparedness in urban centres of Blantyre, Zomba, Lilongwe and Mzuzu in Malawi enabled by context-specific interventions at community, city and national levels, and establishment of an early warning systems for early action. Specifically, the project aims to “contribute to the reduction of risk of injuries, deaths and property loss/damage from disasters suffered by the population of Blantyre, Zomba, Lilongwe and Mzuzu cities by 2024."
The project will: • Undertake risk assessments using the participatory approach, i.e., the City Resilience Action Planning Tool. • Develop, adapt, and test multi-hazard contingency plans incorporating environmental risk mitigation; identify and test evacuation routes • Establish an automated community-based early warning systems (CBEWS)and design a mobile application for dissemination of warnings. • Develop a national urban action plan and strategy to mainstream Disaster Preparedness (DP) and resilience building in urban planning and development and enhance stakeholder engagement. • Strengthen protection mechanisms through training for government officers and communities, establish complaint and feedback mechanisms, and strengthen SRSPS. • Clear solid waste in drainage networks and rehabilitate drainage networks in Blantyre, Zomba, Lilongwe and Mzuzu Cities • Provide emergency contingency stocks for effective response • Activate and implement the crisis modifier for households affected by disasters
